rationale: The run produced all four three-state coefficients for the employment-population ratio (full sample) in output/table2.json under emp_pop_ratio.full: UE=1.0397, IE=0.6435, EU=0.4202, EI=-0.3129. Compared to paper values (UE 1.05, IE 0.69, EU 0.37, EI -0.36): UE matches within 1.0% relative error, but IE is off by 6.7%, EU by 13.6%, and EI by 13.1% — three of four fall outside the 5% match band yet all sit comfortably within the 30% partial band. The qualitative core of the claim reproduces: UE is by far the largest determinant (1.04), IE is the second (0.64), and the two exit rates roughly cancel (EU 0.42 largely offset by EI -0.31, netting +0.11, small relative to UE), matching the paper's stated near-cancellation. Note the reproduced sample span is 1967.25-2004.75 (per table2.json 'sample_span') rather than the paper's full 1967-2010, which likely explains part of the ~13% gap in the exit-rate magnitudes. Overall the pattern and the headline UE coefficient reproduce well but the exit-rate and IE magnitudes deviate beyond the match threshold, warranting a partial verdict.
